beats.label: S1 · A jet lands dead at JFK
beats.text: A jet lands dead at JFK carrying an ornate coffin. Pawnbroker Setrakian warns the CDC to destroy it; his warning is ignored and the coffin slips into the city.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes the arrival of the Master and the failure that lets the plague spread — the inciting event for the whole series.

beats.label: S1 · The old man's war
beats.text: Setrakian survived a Nazi camp where the Master fed on prisoners under officer Eichhorst — now the Master's lieutenant in New York, and Setrakian's lifelong prey.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Grounds why Setrakian knows exactly what this is, and makes Eichhorst the personal antagonist for the rest of the show.

beats.label: S1 · The pawnshop team
beats.text: At Setrakian's pawnshop, Eph, Nora, exterminator Vasiliy Fet and hacker Dutch Velders coalesce into an ad hoc hunting party under the old man's command.
beats.whyLoadBearing: This ensemble is the core cast for the next three seasons; the reader needs to know how and why they came together.

beats.label: S1 · Kelly turns
beats.text: Kelly, Eph's ex-wife, is infected and fully turned. The Master claims her personally and sends her to hunt down their son Zach.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Kelly's turn is the emotional engine of Eph's arc for the rest of the series and sets up Zach as the Master's prize.

beats.label: S1 · Palmer's bargain
beats.text: Palmer bankrolled the Master's arrival in exchange for immortality. When the Master restores him it is only to health — the promised gift withheld.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The grievance seeded here becomes Palmer's eventual defection in S3; without it, the political turn later doesn't land.

beats.label: S1 · The sun does not kill him
beats.text: The team ambushes the Master in Bolivar's theater and drives him into daylight — but he only burns and escapes. Sunlight, the one certainty, does not kill him.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The show's central problem: the old vampire rules don't apply. Every subsequent plan must invent a new way to kill the Master.

beats.label: S1 · The Ancients' human
beats.text: Rebel vampires led by Vaun kidnap ex-con Gus Elizalde and deliver him to the Ancients — a rival strigoi faction who want the Master dead for breaking their truce.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces the second vampire faction and Gus as their human weapon; the whole S2 Quinlan-and-Ancients thread branches from here.

cliffhanger.text: The Master survived sunlight and escaped with his lieutenants intact. Palmer's promised immortality has been reduced to a single dose of health, and the Ancients have just recruited Gus to hunt the Master themselves.
questions: Who are the Ancients, and can they succeed where Setrakian's hunters have failed?
Now that Palmer knows the Master lied about immortality, will he stay loyal?
With Kelly turned and hunting Zach, how does Eph shield his son from his own mother?

characters.name: Ephraim 'Eph' Goodweather
characters.line: CDC lead who exposed the outbreak; framed for murder and now a wanted fugitive running the underground hunting party.

characters.name: Abraham Setrakian
characters.line: 94-year-old Harlem pawnbroker and Nazi camp survivor whose life's mission is killing the Master and Eichhorst.

characters.name: Nora Martinez
characters.line: CDC scientist, Eph's colleague and lover; sheltering her dementia-stricken mother in the pawnshop.

characters.name: Vasiliy Fet
characters.line: City exterminator whose sewer work first exposed the vampires; now the group's demolitionist and soldier.

characters.name: Dutch Velders
characters.line: Hacker who crashed New York's communications for Palmer, then defected to Setrakian's group.

characters.name: Kelly Goodweather
characters.line: Eph's ex-wife, fully turned and personally claimed by the Master to hunt down their son Zach.

characters.name: The Master
characters.line: Ancient vampire whose body arrived in the JFK coffin; escaped daylight only burned, and remains at large.

characters.name: Thomas Eichhorst
characters.line: The Master's Nazi-era lieutenant, a former camp officer, and Setrakian's lifelong nemesis.

characters.name: Eldritch Palmer
characters.line: Elderly billionaire who bankrolled the Master's arrival for immortality; restored only to health, now distrustful.

characters.name: Gus Elizalde
characters.line: Ex-con just recruited by the Ancients — a rival strigoi faction — to serve as their human weapon against the Master.

beats.label: S2 · Feelers and a wounded god
beats.text: Burned and dying in his current body, the Master orders Eichhorst to create Feelers — psychic vampire children — and hands them to Kelly to hunt down Zach.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces the Feelers as Kelly's tool for the rest of the show and sets the Master's weakened state that drives the body-transfer arc.

beats.label: S2 · The Occido Lumen
beats.text: Setrakian identifies a legendary book, the Occido Lumen, that supposedly holds the method to kill the Master. He and Palmer race to find it.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The Lumen is the season's MacGuffin and carries into S3 as the source of the sarcophagus plan.

beats.label: S2 · The bioweapon
beats.text: Eph and Nora develop a bioweapon that kills strigoi. Eph takes it to Washington to arrange production, but a Palmer assassin kills his contact and drives him home.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Eph's science-based approach becomes his signature contribution through S3-S4 and the reason the government looks for him.

beats.label: S2 · Quinlan arrives
beats.text: An ancient half-human, half-strigoi named Quinlan arrives in New York, hunting the Master for personal reasons.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Quinlan becomes the sword arm of the hunters and the only being physically capable of matching the Master in S3-S4.

beats.label: S2 · The Battle of Red Hook
beats.text: Councilwoman Justine Feraldo fortifies Red Hook. When the Master's army storms it her forces annihilate them, and she rises to become the city's new security head.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Feraldo's rise makes her the political ally who runs New York's defense in S3, including Central Park and the bioweapon push.

beats.label: S2 · The Master takes Bolivar
beats.text: With his host body failing, the Master transfers his essence into rock star Bolivar's body — humiliating Eichhorst, who expected to be chosen.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes body-transfer as the Master's survival trick — critical because he does it again in S3 — and cracks the Master-Eichhorst bond.

beats.label: S2 · The train ambush
beats.text: Setrakian wins the Lumen at auction. On a train out of the city Kelly ambushes them — Nora is infected and kills herself; Kelly takes Zach to the Master.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Nora's death and Zach's capture set Eph's entire S3-S4 motivation; the team enters S3 grieving and short-handed.

cliffhanger.text: Setrakian finally holds the Occido Lumen, the key to killing the Master, but Nora is dead and Zach has been carried off to the Master's side. Palmer has been betrayed by the Master and is dying without another dose of the rejuvenating white.
questions: Can Setrakian decode the Lumen and turn its knowledge into action before the Master rebuilds?
What will the Master do with Zach, and can Eph ever get him back?
With Palmer wounded by betrayal, will he stay in the Master's camp or defect to the hunters?

characters.name: Ephraim 'Eph' Goodweather
characters.line: Grieving Nora and consumed with recovering Zach; back from a failed Washington trip and out of allies in government.

characters.name: Abraham Setrakian
characters.line: Won the Occido Lumen at auction; extending his life with strigoi-worm eye drops to see the fight through.

characters.name: Vasiliy Fet
characters.line: Hardened field operative and demolitionist; recently ended a fraught relationship with Dutch.

characters.name: Dutch Velders
characters.line: Fully embedded with the hunters, tortured by Eichhorst and now inseparable from the group.

characters.name: Kelly Goodweather
characters.line: The Master's most loyal servant; now able to pass as human with prosthetics, and holding Zach.

characters.name: Zach Goodweather
characters.line: Eph's son, taken by Kelly on the train and delivered to the Master.

characters.name: The Master
characters.line: Transferred into rock star Bolivar's body after his previous form failed; still hunting Setrakian.

characters.name: Thomas Eichhorst
characters.line: Humiliated by not being chosen as the new host body, still the Master's lieutenant and Setrakian's target.

characters.name: Eldritch Palmer
characters.line: Allied with the Master and dependent on doses of the white; the Master just killed his lover Coco to punish his double-cross.

characters.name: Quinlan
characters.line: Millennia-old human-vampire hybrid working with the Ancients to hunt the Master for his own reasons.

characters.name: Justine Feraldo
characters.line: Red Hook's defender, now the city's special director of security and a public hero.

characters.name: Gus Elizalde
characters.line: Ex-con soldier working with Quinlan and the Ancients against the Master.

beats.label: S3 · Bioweapon and a father searching
beats.text: Months on, Feraldo runs NYC while Eph refines his bioweapon and searches for Zach. Kelly offers to trade the boy for the Occido Lumen.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes where each side stands at season open and the exchange offer that becomes the vehicle for the Master ambush.

beats.label: S3 · Quinlan is the Master's son
beats.text: Quinlan reveals he is the Master's own half-strigoi son, conceived when the Master infected his pregnant mother. Killing the Master will kill him too.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The origin sets Quinlan's stake and the cost of his mission — the price he ultimately pays in the finale.

beats.label: S3 · A kill that isn't a kill
beats.text: During the exchange, Quinlan beheads the Master — but a crimson worm carrying his essence crawls from the corpse and escapes, leaving the war unfinished.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The apparent victory that isn't; makes the body-transfer to Palmer inevitable and defines the remaining fight.

beats.label: S3 · Palmer defects
beats.text: Palmer, deteriorating without the Master's white essence, defects to Setrakian. Setrakian gives him a single dose to keep him upright as an inside informant.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The political turning point — Palmer's access to Stoneheart becomes the tool that sets up the sarcophagus trap.

beats.label: S3 · Central Park falls, nukes arrive
beats.text: Feraldo's assault on Central Park is crushed and the NYPD abandons the city. Eichhorst smuggles two Russian nuclear warheads into New York on a shipment from Egypt.
beats.whyLoadBearing: New York collapses politically at the same moment the weapon that ends the world is being quietly delivered.

beats.label: S3 · The Master takes Palmer
beats.text: Setrakian builds a silver-lined sarcophagus to trap the Master. When they lure him to Stoneheart, the Master transfers his essence into Palmer's body first.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Palmer's body becomes the Master's host — the form he wears into S4 — and Palmer is functionally dead.

beats.label: S3 · Illumination Day
beats.text: They trap the Master. Kelly corners Eph and he kills her; a grief-stricken Zach detonates the remaining nuke, freeing the Master and darkening the sun for good.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The single event that resets the world — sunlight is neutralised, the Master is loose, and Zach is fully lost to the vampires.

cliffhanger.text: Zach's nuclear detonation freed the Master from the silver sarcophagus and blotted out the sun. Eichhorst has taken Zach, the strigoi can now walk freely in daylight, and Setrakian's survivors are scattered underground amid the fallout.
questions: With sunlight blocked, how can humans fight a strigoi enemy no longer bound to the shadows?
Where has Eichhorst taken Zach, and what does the Master want with him?
What kind of world will crawl out of the nuclear fallout — and who will be running it?

characters.name: Ephraim 'Eph' Goodweather
characters.line: Drinking heavily; just killed his own turned wife in self-defense and lost Zach to Eichhorst.

characters.name: Abraham Setrakian
characters.line: Team leader; translated the Lumen and engineered the sarcophagus trap that ultimately failed.

characters.name: Vasiliy Fet
characters.line: Setrakian's right hand and field operative, closely bonded with the group.

characters.name: Dutch Velders
characters.line: Built the strigoi disruption device with Eph, and briefly involved with him.

characters.name: Zach Goodweather
characters.line: Detonated the world-ending nuke in vengeance for Kelly's death; taken by Eichhorst.

characters.name: The Master
characters.line: Original body killed by Quinlan, essence now inhabiting Eldritch Palmer's body; freed by the blast, walking in daylight.

characters.name: Thomas Eichhorst
characters.line: The Master's lieutenant; escorted Zach away as the bomb went off.

characters.name: Quinlan
characters.line: The Master's half-strigoi son, firmly allied with the hunters after severing ties with the Ancients.

characters.name: Gus Elizalde
characters.line: Human soldier for Quinlan; sole survivor of Feraldo's final rearguard in the streets.

characters.name: Justine Feraldo
characters.line: NYC's security director whose Central Park offensive collapsed; killed in a strigoi street ambush as the city fell.

beats.label: S4 · The Partnership
beats.text: Nine months later, strigoi rule the nuclear-blighted world through a collaborator regime called The Partnership. Fet and Quinlan hunt North Dakota for a nuclear warhead.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes the new global order and the plan — a second nuke — that will drive the whole season.

beats.label: S4 · Scattered survivors
beats.text: Hiding in Philadelphia, Eph joins a resistance cell led by Alex. Dutch is trapped in a Partnership facility harvesting B+ women for their blood and infants.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Places the two remaining protagonists in their opening states and sets up their eventual convergence in New York.

beats.label: S4 · New Horizons Farms
beats.text: Eph and Alex discover 'New Horizons Farms' — concentration camps where humans are penned as livestock for strigoi consumption.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Reveals what The Partnership is actually for and gives the season its moral urgency beyond killing the Master.

beats.label: S4 · Setrakian settles his war
beats.text: Dutch escapes with Setrakian and the group reunites in New York. Setrakian poisons Eichhorst with his own blood, beheads him, then asks Quinlan to end him.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The old antagonists die together, closing the S1-era feud and clearing the board for a Master-vs-hunters endgame.

beats.label: S4 · Zach's betrayal
beats.text: Reunited with Eph, Zach lies about his loyalty and bait-traps his father for the Feelers. Realizing the betrayal, Eph still can't bring himself to kill his son.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Confirms Zach is fully the Master's creature and sets the emotional terms of the final confrontation.

beats.label: S4 · The Master takes Eph
beats.text: Fet and Quinlan lure the Master into a tunnel with the nuke. The Master transfers into Eph's body — but Eph arms the bomb before losing control.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The final gambit; Eph's last act ensures the Master's new body is also his tomb.

beats.label: S4 · The end and after
beats.text: Zach triggers the bomb, killing the Master and himself. Five years on, the nuclear winter fades — Fet and Dutch reunite, Gus resettles refugees, humanity has won.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The series resolution; states plainly who survived and what kind of world they emerged into.

cliffhanger.text: The Master and his lieutenants are dead. Eph, Setrakian, Quinlan and Zach paid the price, and five years on the nuclear winter is receding — the survivors are quietly rebuilding what was lost.
questions: Can a poisoned Earth ever truly recover, or is the fade only cosmetic?
With the last strigoi held captive, how long before the world grows careless about the ones that remain?
Do Fet and Dutch's reunion, and Gus's resettlement work, add up to a future worth the cost?

characters.name: Ephraim 'Eph' Goodweather
characters.line: Killed in the final blast; his body had been possessed by the Master when Eph armed the bomb.

characters.name: Vasiliy Fet
characters.line: Alive at the end; led the nuke plan into Manhattan and reunites with Dutch as the world thaws.

characters.name: Dutch Velders
characters.line: Escaped the breeding facility; five years on, helping rebuild the internet.

characters.name: Abraham Setrakian
characters.line: Killed mid-season, but not before poisoning and beheading Eichhorst — his life's mission finally complete.

characters.name: Quinlan
characters.line: The Master's half-strigoi son; mortally wounded luring the Master into the final trap.

characters.name: Zach Goodweather
characters.line: Turned back to humanity at the last moment; detonated the final bomb, killing himself and the Master.

characters.name: The Master
characters.line: Destroyed in the final nuclear blast along with Eph's body, ending the strigoi hierarchy.

characters.name: Thomas Eichhorst
characters.line: Killed by Setrakian's poisoned blood and beheaded in their long-delayed final meeting.

characters.name: Gus Elizalde
characters.line: Alive; his wartime black-market network became postwar refugee resettlement.
